subject: Culture
title: How Languages Die
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How Languages Die.

hook.text: A language dies every two weeks. By 2100, half of the world's 7,000 languages will be gone.

buildup.text: Languages die when parents stop teaching them to children, usually because a dominant language offers more opportunity.

discovery.text: UNESCO classifies languages from 'safe' to 'extinct.' Over 2,500 are currently endangered.

twist.text: A language doesn't need zero speakers to die. It needs zero children learning it.

climax.text: Each dead language takes unique ecological knowledge, medicinal plants, and oral histories with it forever.

punchline.text: A language is a library that burns quietly.

quiz.question: How often does a language die on average?

details.summary: A language dies when its last fluent speaker dies — and this happens roughly every two weeks. Of the world's approximately 7,000 languages, nearly half are endangered.
details.whyItMatters: Each language death destroys a unique way of understanding the world, including ecological knowledge, medicinal practices, and mathematical concepts that exist nowhere else.
takeaways: A language dies approximately every two weeks
Nearly half of the world's 7,000 languages are endangered
Most language death results from political and economic pressure, not choice

faq.question: How do languages die?
faq.answer: Languages die through a predictable process: first, the dominant language controls education, government, and commerce. Parents stop teaching children the minority language because it offers no economic advantage. The language becomes restricted to elderly speakers and ceremonial use.

faq.question: Why should we care about language death?
faq.answer: Each language encodes unique knowledge — Indigenous languages contain botanical, ecological, and medicinal information unknown to science. Languages contain mathematical and philosophical concepts that other languages lack. Language diversity drives cognitive diversity.
